spoken: Long call breakeven: strike plus premium. Calls up.
Long put breakeven: strike minus premium. Puts down.

front: Max loss for any option buyer
spoken: An option buyer can lose only the premium paid.
A naked call writer has unlimited risk, because the stock can rise without limit.

back: (Strike - premium) x 100: stock goes to zero.
spoken: A naked put writer's worst case is the stock going to zero: strike minus premium, times one hundred.
A call is in the money when the market is above the strike.
A put is in the money when the market is below the strike.
Time value equals premium minus intrinsic value.
Bullish positions: long calls and short puts.
Bearish positions: long puts and short calls.

front: Protective put: breakeven and max loss
back: BE = stock cost + premium. Max loss = (cost - strike + premium) x 100.
spoken: Protective put breakeven is stock cost plus premium. Max loss is cost minus strike, plus premium.

front: Covered call: breakeven and max gain
back: BE = stock cost - premium. Max gain = (strike - cost + premium) x 100.
spoken: Covered call breakeven is stock cost minus premium. Max gain is strike minus cost, plus premium.

front: Best hedge for a short stock position
back: Buy a call (full protection). Selling a put gives only partial protection.
spoken: To hedge short stock, buy a call. Selling a put only gives partial protection, equal to the premium.
Call spread breakeven: lower strike plus the net premium.
Put spread breakeven: higher strike minus the net premium.
Debit spread max gain: the difference between strikes minus the net debit.
Credit spread max loss: the difference between strikes minus the net credit.

back: Debit spreads want premiums to WIDEN. Credit spreads want them to NARROW or expire.
spoken: Debit widen, credit narrow. D W C N.
Straddle breakevens: strike plus and minus the total of both premiums.
A long straddle buyer expects a big move but doesn't know which way.
Index options settle in cash: intrinsic value times the one hundred dollar multiplier.

back: Same number of contracts; more shares per contract; strike reduced so total value stays equal.
spoken: For an uneven split, you keep the same number of contracts, but each covers more shares at a lower strike. Total value stays the same.
Exercising a long call: your stock cost basis is strike plus premium.
An assigned call writer's sale proceeds are strike plus premium.
Taxable equivalent yield: divide the muni yield by one minus the tax rate.

back: 30/360, from last coupon date up to but not including settlement.
spoken: Munis use thirty three sixty, counting up to the day before settlement.

back: Premium must be amortized; basis falls to par; no deductible loss at maturity.
spoken: Muni premiums must be amortized. Hold to maturity and there's no gain or loss, and no deduction.

back: OID accretes tax-exempt; secondary-market discount is generally ordinary income.
spoken: Original issue discount on a muni accretes tax-free. Market discount is generally taxed as ordinary income.
Debt service coverage: net revenues divided by annual debt service.

back: Net: operations and maintenance paid first. Gross: debt service paid first.
spoken: In a net revenue pledge, operations and maintenance come first. In a gross pledge, debt service comes first.

back: Repaid from a future bond issue, taxes, other revenues, grants.
spoken: BANs are repaid by bonds, TANs by taxes, RANs by revenues, and GANs by grants.

back: Revenue bond also backed by the issuer's taxing power; rated like a GO.
spoken: A double-barreled bond has revenues plus taxing power behind it, so it's rated like a GO.
For a discount bond, nominal is lowest, then current yield, then yield to maturity, and yield to call is highest.

back: Bond price / conversion ratio. Ratio = $1,000 / conversion price.
spoken: Parity stock price is bond price divided by the conversion ratio. The ratio is a thousand divided by the conversion price.

back: Loss disallowed if substantially identical securities (incl. calls) are bought 30 days before or after the sale.
spoken: A wash sale disallows a loss if you buy the same stock, or a call on it, within thirty days before or after.

back: Inherited: stepped up to value at death, always long-term. Gift (appreciated): donor's basis and holding period carry over.
spoken: Inherited stock steps up to the value at death and is always long-term. Gifted stock keeps the donor's basis.
Cum rights value: market minus subscription price, divided by rights plus one.
Sales charge percent: offering price minus N A V, divided by the offering price.

back: 13 months, backdate up to 90 days, non-binding.
spoken: A letter of intent gives thirteen months to hit a breakpoint, can be backdated ninety days, and isn't binding.

back: Return > AIR: payment up. Return = AIR: same. Return < AIR: down.
spoken: If the separate account beats the AIR, the next payment rises. Equal, it stays flat. Below, it falls.
Annuity withdrawals come out earnings first, as ordinary income, with a ten percent penalty before fifty-nine and a half.
Quick ratio: current assets minus inventory, over current liabilities.

back: $19,000 per recipient ($38,000 with gift splitting). Changes yearly; verify current year.
spoken: For twenty twenty-six, the annual gift exclusion is nineteen thousand per recipient, or thirty-eight thousand for a couple splitting gifts. This changes over time.

back: Validate within 1 business day; complete within 3 business days after validation.
spoken: ACATS: validate in one business day, complete in three more.
